recommendation.reason: Multiple mature, MIT-licensed tools already generate typed TypeScript clients from OpenAPI 3.x offline in CI. openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch matches the plan's must-haves and directly satisfies the CI staleness requirement via --check; building would duplicate a solved, high-maturity problem the user prefers to adopt.
recommendation.reusableOption: openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch (openapi-ts/openapi-typescript, MIT). Pair with orval if axios or React Query hooks are later required.
recommendation.biggestUnknown: Whether the team's specs use split/multi-file $ref that needs a Redocly bundle step before generation; no leading tool exposes this as a native CLI flag.

notableDesigns.title: --check for CI drift
notableDesigns.detail: Verifies generated types match the source spec and exits non-zero on drift, directly satisfying the plan's staleness-fail step.

notableDesigns.title: Thin fetch client
notableDesigns.detail: openapi-fetch wraps native fetch at 6 kB with type-safe body/query/path/response, keeping the runtime footprint minimal.

reusableLessons: Separate type generation (openapi-typescript) from the client (openapi-fetch) so teams can adopt either independently.
Ship a --check mode that diffs generated output against the spec to enforce no-drift in CI.
competitors.summary: Closest fit to the plan's must-haves and the only leading tool with a native CI staleness flag; adopt instead of building.
competitors.coverageNote: Capabilities verified against openapi-ts.dev CLI, advanced, and openapi-fetch docs (2026-08-29).
